summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of breast cancer, gastroparesis, and a GJ tube presented for a left total mastectomy due to recurrent invasive lobular carcinoma in the upper-inner quadrant, ER/PR positive and HER2 negative. The surgery was uncomplicated, and she was admitted for overnight observation. Pain was managed with acetaminophen and tramadol to avoid exacerbating gastroparesis. She tolerated a clear diet postoperatively and advanced to a regular diet, remained afebrile, and was ambulating well. A single JP drain was placed, and visiting nurse services were arranged for home care. She was discharged on postoperative day one with instructions for wound and drain care, activity restrictions, and a follow-up appointment in one week. Final pathology is pending, and further oncologic treatment will be determined in consultation with medical oncology.
problems: Malignant neoplasm of upper-inner quadrant of left female breast
Other artificial openings of gastrointestinal tract status
Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture
